title: ALS, myasthenia gravis, CIDP and muscular dystrophy
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's neuromuscular condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Leg weakness

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 54-year-old male with a known history of Becker muscular dystrophy. He presents for a follow-up regarding slowly progressive leg weakness. He reports that his mobility has decreased over the last six months, noting increased difficulty with stairs and longer distances. He currently utilizes a cane for stability during ambulation. He denies any new onset of upper extremity weakness or significant changes in his respiratory status.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Neuromuscular: Positive (lower extremity weakness)
Respiratory: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Positive (lower extremity gait changes)
All other systems: Negative

Medication List:
- Physical therapy exercises (daily)
- Multivitamin

Exam:
General: Well-appearing male in no acute distress.
Neuromuscular: Notable for proximal muscle weakness in bilateral lower extremities. Gait is steady but slow, requiring a cane for support. Strength is 4/5 in hip flexion and knee extension. No significant changes in upper extremity strength noted.

Assessment:
1. Becker muscular dystrophy presenting with slowly progressive leg weakness.

Plan:
1. Continue current physical therapy regimen focusing on lower extremity mobility.
2. Patient to continue using cane for safety during ambulation.
3. Return to clinic in 6 months for reassessment of motor function.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Becker muscular dystrophy shares a code with Duchenne: G71.01 (HCC 197).
